text:
You need a set of cannabis-themed AI art concepts for a new dispensary in Illinois that can be printed on acrylic boards and refined after an initial round of idea generation.

I’m Noor Halden, and I’d be a strong fit for this because I have 6 years of experience working with Python and machine learning tools, including PyTorch, scikit-learn, LangChain, OpenAI API, Hugging Face Transformers, NLP, XGBoost, and pandas. While my background is technical rather than traditional illustration, I’ve worked on AI-driven systems where clear concept generation, structured iteration, and quality control mattered a lot.

One relevant project was a contract clause search assistant for a legal client. I built an assistant that answers questions over 9,000 contracts and always quotes the clause and page it used. Using Python, LangChain, OpenAI API, pgvector, PostgreSQL, and FastAPI, the system achieved 0.91 faithfulness on a 120-question lawyer-written test set, and it reduced clause lookup time from 25 minutes to 3 minutes. That project taught me how to develop outputs that are useful, traceable, and easy to refine based on feedback.

For your dispensary, I’d approach the first 30 minutes as a concept sprint: generating a broad set of rough directions around cannabis, terpenes, smoke, and any more abstract or experimental visual themes that fit a large retail space. I’d focus on variety first so you can quickly react to different directions, then narrow toward the strongest concepts for further refinement. Since you’re looking for art to hang throughout a large space, I’d think in terms of cohesive series as well as standout pieces.

I understand you’d like to review an AI-generated art portfolio as part of the selection process. If helpful, I can also keep the concepts organized by theme so it’s easier to decide which ideas should be developed further.

Would you like the first round of concepts to lean more toward bold, modern dispensary visuals, or more abstract and atmospheric art?
